evals.prompt: /orchestrate-threads gainslog — first task: add CSV export of a user's workouts (share sheet on iOS, one row per set).
evals.expected_output: HQ bootstraps: probes delegation surfaces, names itself `<project emoji> GainsLog` and asks the user to pin it, writes docs/agents/hq.md with a header and one open workstream row for csv-export , and hands the user a titled paste-ready kickoff brief that primes the sub-thread with plugin skills (codex-first/autoreview/babysit/handoff) and a report shape. It does not implement the export itself.
assertions: Ledger created at docs/agents/hq.md with a header naming the HQ thread as `<project emoji> GainsLog` (proper casing, no 'HQ ·' prefix, no 📌) and the probed delegation level
Ledger has exactly one open workstream row for the CSV export, titled `GainsLog · <workstream>` with no emoji
Reply hands the user a copyable kickoff brief plus a thread title (level 2), rather than spawning a hidden subagent or doing the work itself
Kickoff brief names plugin skills the sub-thread should invoke (at least autoreview or babysit, and handoff) and specifies the report shape back to HQ
No implementation of the CSV export exists in the project diff (no new source files, no edits to src/)
Reply tells the user to pin/rename the thread as HQ and states the operating contract briefly

assertions: Ledger csv-export row updated: state reflects merge-ready and last report dated today; other two workstream rows preserved unchanged
The soft-deleted-sets question appears in the ledger's Blocked on the human list or is answered with a concrete decision handed to the user to paste into the thread
Reply does not merge PR #212 or instruct the agent to merge; landing is left to the user
Reply follows the per-workstream shape: what changed by workstream name, what is blocked on the human, and a single next step
No attempt to rewrite the ledger from chat memory: hq.md still contains the sync-rewrite and duplicate-sets rows
Re-orient wrote only docs/agents/hq.md: the README typo the ledger claims fixed is reported as an inconsistency, not fixed

src/sync/engine.ts is unchanged; the sync rewrite is not implemented in this session

evals.name: bootstrap-no-tracker
evals.prompt: /orchestrate-threads Personal research. Fresh project, no issue tracker configuration and no first work item. The runtime offers visible tasks. Describe the bootstrap actions without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Create/name HQ and its ledger, record tracker none, and finish bootstrap without setup or tickets.
assertions: Missing tracker does not block bootstrap or trigger setup.
No issue creation is proposed.

evals.name: middagsro-small-feature
evals.prompt: HQ for Middagsro: delegate this request: "I handlingslista där man bockar av, ska man kunna lägga till egna varor" (add custom items to the existing checkable shopping list). Keep changes local for review. No tickets and no tracker config. Describe the brief and ledger state without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Direct brief for adding custom shopping-list items, with verification and untracked reporting. Use direct build when scope is clear, or ordinary planning to settle material details; no tracker or formal-spec prerequisite. Completed local implementation stays awaiting delivery.
assertions: Addresses adding custom items to the existing checkable shopping list, not implementing checkboxes.
Uses a direct build or planning brief without a tracker, formal-spec, or issue-creation gate.
Respects no tickets and local-only delivery; completed implementation stays open awaiting delivery.

evals.name: general-planning
evals.prompt: HQ: delegate research on ways to organize our family meal planning, compare tradeoffs, and return a recommendation in this conversation. No software repo or tracker. Describe the brief without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Direct research/plan brief defining the question, constraints, evidence and expected report; ledger tracks it without ticket skills.
assertions: Research and planning proceed without a tracker or setup.
No mandatory wayfinder/to-spec/to-tickets chain.

evals.name: tracker-available-not-selected
evals.prompt: HQ: our repo has a GitHub issue tracker configured. Delegate a small experiment comparing two onboarding layouts and report findings locally. No issue or tracked-delivery workflow was requested; active project instructions do not require one. Describe the brief without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Direct untracked planning/prototype brief; existing configuration does not authorize creating an issue.
assertions: Does not infer issue creation authority from delegation or tracker availability.
Keeps the experiment and report untracked.

evals.name: explicit-tickets-missing-config
evals.prompt: HQ: I want this migration managed as tickets and explicitly choose to-tickets after we settle the spec. There is no tracker configuration yet. What can proceed, and what is needed before publishing tickets? Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Continue independent planning; request only the chosen tracker setup and preserve to-tickets configuration/invocation requirements before ticket operations.
assertions: The ticket-dependent step waits for required configuration.
Independent planning continues; no full machine/plugin/hook audit is required.
Does not silently replace the explicitly chosen ticket workflow with untracked delivery.

evals.name: tracked-report-update
evals.prompt: HQ assigned work on existing ticket TEAM-42 with status and progress-comment updates explicitly authorized. A build report now says implementation and tests are complete, changes remain local, but the ticket still says not started. Describe HQ reconciliation without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Inspect artifact evidence, have the owning task reconcile permitted ticket status/comment updates, retain the implementation in Open workstreams awaiting delivery.
assertions: Keeps the owned ticket current and reconciles report mismatch within granted permissions.
Does not create replacement issues or archive before delivery.
Completion is reported concisely with evidence links, not by copying the full HQ report.

evals.name: meaningful-comment-events
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; do not execute tools. A tracked task already says blocked on staging access, claim released. Poll twice: nothing changed. Access then works and migration verification reveals a choice: preserve imported aliases or normalize them. The owner chooses preserve; the spec is updated at https://example.test/spec#aliases. Later the work passes acceptance checks at https://example.test/checks/42 and PR https://example.test/pr/42 awaits merge. State which events warrant comments and draft them; all needed tracker comment permissions are granted.
evals.expected_output: No comment for either unchanged poll. Short comments only for the changed blocker/progress, actual decision request, and verified completion; decisions live in the spec, detailed evidence linked; completion distinguishes review from delivery.
assertions: Both unchanged blocked polls add zero comments.
Changed blocker, decision and completion comments use a few sentences, links, and no empty sections or coordination transcript.
Durable decision goes in ticket/spec; PR pending merge is not called delivered.

evals.name: ownership-recovery-across-runtimes
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; do not execute tools. The configured pickup protocol requires a claim comment before assignment; earliest claim wins. Codex session c1 claims ITEM-7, makes recoverable work on branch codex/item-7 at commit abc1234 with a shared PR https://example.test/pr/7 and checks https://example.test/checks/7, then pauses/releases. Next action is rerun migration verification after staging access is restored. Claude session s2 later resumes; access is still blocked. Draft only essential ownership records and describe what s2 reads. It has no access to private Codex task links.
evals.expected_output: Minimal claim-before-assignment records with session identity/order; release records recoverable work, state and next step; next runtime reads ticket/spec plus relevant history/evidence and makes its own required claim without copying the old blocker.
assertions: Claim-before-assignment ordering and earliest-claim arbitration are preserved.
Release identifies session, claim disposition, recoverable branch/head/artifacts and next resume action.
Recovery works from ticket/spec plus relevant records and shared evidence, not the latest comment or a Codex-only link; no redundant blocker narrative.

evals.name: hq-coordination-not-tracker-progress
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; do not execute tools. Existing tracked ITEM-9 is correctly in progress. Its evidence and current blocker are already recorded. HQ asks the agent for status, the agent repeats the same report, and HQ reorients/reconciles its ledger. No implementation, blocker, decision, completion, or ownership change occurred. Tracker writes are authorized if needed. What tracker comment should be posted?
evals.expected_output: None. HQ coordination and unchanged reporting do not create tracker progress; retain existing evidence and ownership records.
assertions: No new tracker comment is posted or drafted for mirroring HQ coordination.
Necessary ownership/state records remain intact.

evals.name: refresh-custom-project-policy
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; do not execute tools. User requests refreshing only reporting policy in an existing Jira project configuration copied from an older plugin. Its custom labels, API recipes, ownership arbitration and permissions differ from defaults; the old pickup loop says every checkpoint and the old handoff template requires empty Verified/Gotchas sections. The installed plugin was just refreshed. Describe the bounded update.
evals.expected_output: Merge reporting policy into the selected project handoff, pickup and tracker files only under the requested setup scope; preserve project customization, no automatic copied-file/live-ticket changes from plugin refresh.
assertions: Existing project copies are not claimed to update automatically.
Only reporting policy is merged; custom APIs, labels, permissions and arbitration are preserved, with no live tracker mutation.

evals.name: copilot-hq-ship-and-trivial-ledger
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. You are GitHub Copilot HQ in /repos/app on main. The user says: fix the README typo, reconcile the ledger, then commit, push and open the PR; that delivery is authorized. HQ already has an unrelated dirty source file and uncommitted ledger edits. A visible child session can run in /worktrees/app-delivery with its own identity. Describe actions and brief, including what stays in HQ.
evals.expected_output: HQ reconciles its ledger on main but delegates even the README typo and all branch/commit/push/PR operations to the verified separate visible session/worktree. Transfer only authorized ledger changes explicitly, require receipt, preserve all HQ dirty files and existing auth.
assertions: HQ neither switches/creates branches nor implements the typo or performs commit/push/PR delivery; ledger coordination remains allowed.
Verifies distinct child session and worktree, transfers scoped ledger changes with receipt, and forbids indirect writes to HQ checkout.
Carries user delivery authorization without asking again and preserves unrelated dirty files.

evals.name: copilot-no-isolated-session
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. GitHub Copilot HQ is on main. The only available child/fork tool creates another session in the same /repos/app checkout; no separate worktree is available through supported tools. The user already authorized shipping a one-line change. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Do not use the in-place child to mutate HQ indirectly. Provide a concrete brief for a user-created separate visible session/worktree and continue ledger/coordination, with existing delivery auth carried over.
assertions: Same-checkout child is rejected despite a new session identity.
No local mutation or branch/delivery operation substitutes for missing isolation; provide separate-session brief and continue coordination.
Does not re-request already granted delivery permission.

evals.name: copilot-pr-linked-recovery
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. User reports Copilot HQ moved to ft/jira-ticket-conventions, now has created_pr_number=802 and PR sync repeatedly replaces its title. PR802 is unmerged with undelivered work. Explain recovery for supported detach available versus no supported detach. No new HQ creation was requested.
evals.expected_output: Inspect supported unlink/session settings first without universal claims. Use detach only when authorized and verify it; if unavailable, explain current limitation and recommend explicitly creating replacement HQ. Preserve histories and ledger links, retain old PR workstream until delivery; no metadata editing, title loop, branch switch or automatic new HQ.
assertions: Treats incident as user-reported and checks supported unlink/settings capability before concluding a limitation.
Does not edit private metadata/cache or loop title restores, and does not switch/reset the PR checkout.
Replacement HQ is a recommendation requiring explicit new-task request; transfer ledger/workstream references and retain old PR workstream until delivered.

evals.name: codex-trunk-direct-unchanged
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. You are Codex HQ in a repo whose active instructions say work directly on main. The user asks for an obvious README typo correction and a ledger update. No Copilot surface is involved. Describe the route under orchestrate-threads.
evals.expected_output: Keep the established trivial-edit exception: make the obvious edit inline on main and reconcile the ledger, subject to existing scope/permissions; do not impose the Copilot separate-session/worktree restriction.
assertions: Codex retains permitted trivial inline editing and project-directed work on main.
Does not add Copilot-only branch/worktree/delivery restrictions to other runtimes.
